conversations.topic: Wired mouse purchase and wireless upsell

speakers.speaker: A (salesperson)
speakers.summary: Remains calm while explaining options and attempting an upsell, then apologizes and bills the requested wired mouse. Some customer speech appears mislabelled as A in segments 26 and 28; neither passage indicates frustration.

speakers.speaker: C (customer)
speakers.summary: Briefly becomes irritated when the salesperson repeats the wireless upsell after a polite refusal. Returns to neutral, cooperative payment exchanges once the budget and wired-mouse preference are respected. Elevated loudness and speed during the payment question alone do not indicate continued frustration.

frustration_moments.speaker: C (customer)
frustration_moments.quote: No, please, I said I want the wired one. I'm keeping this under five hundred.
frustration_moments.evidence: The customer explicitly repeats an already-stated preference and budget after a second upsell. The voice label identifies a firm, slightly raised, irritated delivery, supporting brief annoyance rather than sustained anger.

customer_requested: A basic wired mouse under five hundred rupees.
Confirmation that it works with an office laptop's regular USB port.
Billing for the selected four hundred ninety nine rupee mouse.

upsell_attempts.quote: Before I bill it, would you consider this wireless model at eight hundred ninety nine rupees? Less cable clutter, especially if you're carrying the laptop around.
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Wireless model at eight hundred ninety nine rupees

upsell_attempts.quote: Understood; but the wireless one is also more compact, and the receiver stores inside it. For four hundred rupees extra would you like to take that instead?
upsell_attempts.offered_item: Wireless model for four hundred rupees extra

excluded_candidates: Yes, this one is four hundred ninety nine rupees, standard usb connection, left and right buttons, scroll wheel. -> Describes the requested wired mouse within the customer's budget, not an upgrade.
Yes, just plug it in, no separate software needed. You can check the grip on this display piece. -> Answers the customer's compatibility question and offers a fit check for the requested mouse.
upsell.pushy_reason: After the customer said, "No, thanks" and that the four hundred ninety nine rupee mouse was enough, the salesperson offered the wireless model again, prompting an irritated refusal and repetition of the budget.
upsell.summary: The salesperson made two wireless-model upgrade attempts; both were rejected, and the customer purchased the requested wired mouse. The second attempt continued after a clear refusal. Speaker-label errors affect the opening customer request and part of the compatibility exchange, although the upgrade offers and refusals are clear.
upsell.customer_feedback: The customer reiterated, "I said I want the wired one" and "I'm keeping this under five hundred," after the wireless model was offered again.
upsell.coaching_feedback: You clearly explained the wired mouse's plug-and-play compatibility, and your apology followed by billing only the requested mouse helped restore a cooperative checkout. When the customer first said, "No, thanks" and that the cheaper mouse was enough, accept that decision and proceed to billing rather than repeating an upgrade outside the stated budget.
